SELECT
    CAST(activity_id AS TEXT) AS activity_id,
    CAST(assigned_to_user AS TEXT) AS assigned_user_id,
    CAST(deal_id AS TEXT) AS deal_id,
    CAST(done AS BOOLEAN) AS is_done,
    CAST(due_to AS TIMESTAMP) AS due_to_at,
    CAST(type AS TEXT) AS activity_type_category
FROM "postgres"."public"."activity"

SELECT
    CAST(id AS TEXT) AS activity_type_id,
    CAST(name AS TEXT) AS activity_type_name,
    CAST(type AS TEXT) AS activity_type_category,
    CASE
      WHEN LOWER(active) = 'yes' THEN TRUE
      WHEN LOWER(active) = 'no'  THEN FALSE
        ELSE NULL END
     AS is_active -- convert booalen for simplicity
FROM "postgres"."public"."activity_types"

FROM "postgres"."public"."deal_changes"

-- I need business input to understand changing user_ids in same deal_ids are a data quality issue or part of business
-- I assumed it is part of the business, therefore I aimed to bring as is user_id for each stage in given stage.

with cte_impacted_deals as (
    select distinct deal_id
    from "postgres"."public_crm_staging"."stg_deal_changes"
    
    where changed_at >= current_date - interval '3 day'
    
)


, cte_user_changes as (
    select
        deal_id,
        changed_at as valid_from,
        new_value::int as user_id,
        coalesce(lead(changed_at) over (
            partition by deal_id
            order by changed_at
        ), timestamp '2999-12-31 23:59:59') as valid_to
    from "postgres"."public_crm_staging"."stg_deal_changes"
    where changed_field_key = 'user_id'
    
        and deal_id in (select deal_id from cte_impacted_deals)
     
)


, cte_deal_changes as (
    select
        deal_id,
        changed_at as stage_start_time,
        new_value::int as stage_id,
        changed_field_key,
        lead(changed_at) over (partition by deal_id order by changed_at) as stage_end_time
    from "postgres"."public_crm_staging"."stg_deal_changes"
    where
        changed_field_key in ('stage_id', 'lost_reason')
        -- process only recent activities to reduce volume
    
        and deal_id in (select deal_id from cte_impacted_deals)
     
)

select
    cte_deal_changes.deal_id,
    user_id, -- useful for any location/team/marketing etc. related analyses
    cte_deal_changes.changed_field_key as changed_field_key, -- just bringing to keep incremental logic work
    cte_deal_changes.stage_id,
    case when cte_deal_changes.changed_field_key = 'lost_reason' then concat('Lost - ', field_options.label_value)
         else label_value end as stage_name, -- includes lost deals for future analyses
    case when cte_deal_changes.changed_field_key = 'lost_reason' then true 
         else false end as is_lost_deal,
    cte_deal_changes.stage_start_time,
    cte_deal_changes.stage_end_time,
    cte_deal_changes.stage_end_time::date - cte_deal_changes.stage_start_time::date as stage_duration_in_days -- useful for any funnel analyses and continuous improvement works
from cte_deal_changes
left join cte_user_changes
  on cte_deal_changes.deal_id = cte_user_changes.deal_id
     and cte_deal_changes.stage_start_time >= cte_user_changes.valid_from
     and cte_deal_changes.stage_start_time < cte_user_changes.valid_to
     and (cte_deal_changes.stage_end_time >= cte_user_changes.valid_from or cte_deal_changes.stage_end_time is null)
left join "postgres"."public_crm_intermediate"."int_field_options" as field_options
    on cte_deal_changes.changed_field_key = field_options.field_key
        and cte_deal_changes.stage_id = field_options.label_id

select field_id
from "postgres"."public_crm_intermediate"."int_field_options"
where field_id is null

-- postgres specific, might not work on other engines/databases
select distinct on (deal_id)
    deal_id,
    user_id,
    stage_id,
    stage_name,
    is_lost_deal,
    stage_start_time,
    stage_end_time,
    stage_duration_in_days
from "postgres"."public_crm_intermediate"."int_deal_stages_history"
order by deal_id, stage_start_time desc

select
    distinct deal_stages.deal_id,
    date_trunc('month', stage_start_time)::date AS month_changed, -- this will bring the first day of the month, can be changed the month name etc
    activity_types.activity_type_name,
    CASE
        WHEN activity_types.activity_type_name='Sales Call 1' THEN '2.1'
        WHEN activity_types.activity_type_name='Sales Call 2' THEN '3.1'
        ELSE 'unknown'
    END AS funnel_step
FROM "postgres"."public_crm_intermediate"."int_deal_stages_history" AS deal_stages
JOIN "postgres"."public_crm_intermediate"."int_activity_history" AS activity_history
    ON activity_history.deal_id = deal_stages.deal_id
JOIN "postgres"."public_crm_staging"."stg_activity_types" AS activity_types
    ON activity_types.activity_type_category = activity_history.activity_type_category
WHERE deal_stages.stage_id IN ('2','3')
    and activity_types.activity_type_category IN ('meeting', 'sc_2')
    and deal_stages.is_lost_deal = false

select deal_id
from "postgres"."public_crm_intermediate"."int_deal_stages_history"
where deal_id is null

select deal_id
from "postgres"."public_crm_intermediate"."int_deal_stages_latest"
where deal_id is null

select
    DATE_TRUNC('month', stage_start_time)::date AS month_reported,
    stage_name AS kpi_name,
    stage_id::text AS funnel_step,
    COUNT(distinct deal_id) AS deals_count
from "postgres"."public_crm_intermediate"."int_deal_stages_history"
where is_lost_deal = false
group by 
    month_reported,
    kpi_name,
    funnel_step

UNION ALL

SELECT
    month_changed AS month_reported,
    activity_type_name AS kpi_name,
    funnel_step AS funnel_step,
    COUNT(DISTINCT deal_id) AS deals_count
FROM "postgres"."public_crm_intermediate"."int_sales_call_history"
GROUP BY 
    month_reported,
    kpi_name,
    funnel_step
